Continue Azure IaC (Bicep) migration plan decisions

notes.text: Working through decisions 1-7 (subscription, resource group, infra/ layout, RG inventory, secrets strategy, Front Door key auth timing, CI what-if). Stopped after answering #1 (Azure access/subscription). See pi session 019feaef-a6bd-7c0d-882f-c8fbf043f053 for full discussion/context, reference doc: /home/josh/development/work/huddler/hub/workspace1/docs/azure-iac-migration-plan.md

Decision 1 answered: logged into 'MPN - jhollander' sub (2baa338f-00c0-4e5b-a7c4-ad03e419f6fc), tenant diversus.com.au, access confirmed. Trial RG = HuddlerSubscriptionManager (same sub) containing Function App, Storage, App Insights, Logic Apps, connections, etc. The Front Door itself (HuddlerSubscriptionManagerFrontDoor) lives on 'MPN - devops' sub (7d24c48d-a68e-46b7-9802-ff9d41879d14) inside DWP-PROD RG, which is a SHARED RG with many unrelated resources (other apps' storage/service plans/sites) - so DWP-PROD can't be decompiled wholesale, only the specific Front Door resource. Both subs already available via az account list, no extra login needed.

Decision 2 answered: template scope = ALL resources from HuddlerSubscriptionManager RG (sub 2baa338f-00c0-4e5b-a7c4-ad03e419f6fc) + ONLY the Front Door resource (HuddlerSubscriptionManagerFrontDoor) from DWP-PROD RG (sub 7d24c48d-a68e-46b7-9802-ff9d41879d14) - combined into a SINGLE Bicep template deployable to a single resource group (cross-subscription source, single-RG target). Trial deploy target = 'Huddler-Staging' RG on sub 75f130b6-33d3-4c6a-b2a1-6d8c066df3b5 (MPN - dtang), confirmed empty/clean. Note: this needed a fresh access grant mid-session before az could see the dtang subscription.

Decision 3 answered: Bicep lives at Apps/SubscriptionAndTelemetry/infra/ (an empty infra/ folder already exists there alongside the SubscriptionManager app code) - not a top-level repo infra/ dir. Since it's one combined template, expect a flat-ish layout under that infra/ dir (main.bicep + modules/*.bicep), not per-resource-group folders.

Decision 4 answered: scope is final - HuddlerSubscriptionManager RG + the one Front Door resource is the entire migration target for now. No other resource groups (SharePoint hosting etc.) planned/needed.

Decision 5 answered: secrets strategy = @secure() params (not Key Vault). Investigated actual resources first: currently NO real secrets exist to protect - Function App uses managed identity end-to-end for storage (AzureWebJobsStorage__credential/__clientId, no connection string), App Insights connection string isn't sensitive, and the 4 Logic App API connections (sharepointonline x2, azuretables x2) are OAuth-based tied to joshua.hollander@diversus.com.au (not a static key - needs manual re-auth click in Portal after any deploy regardless of secrets strategy). Policy going forward: use @secure() params for anything that does need a secret later (e.g. future Front Door function key from decision 6).

Decision 6: CORRECTION - the Front Door function-key auth step is ALREADY DONE (I was wrong that it wasn't set up; plan doc was stale). Verified live: route 'default-route' (pattern /*) on endpoint 'subscription-cache' has rule set 'SubscriptionManagerRules' attached, containing rule 'AddFunctionKeyForSubscriptionManager' (UrlPath BeginsWith /api/getSubscriptionData -> Append header x-functions-key with a live key value). Nothing to do manually - just capture this rule set/rule/header-action in the Bicep when templating Front Door, with the key value as a @secure() param per decision 5.

Decision 7 answered: CI what-if on PRs is deferred to future work, to be revisited at the end once the Bicep template itself exists and is proven out. Not needed for the initial migration.

ALL 7 DECISIONS NOW RESOLVED - ready to start actual Bicep work:
1. Subscription/access: logged into MPN - jhollander (2baa338f-00c0-4e5b-a7c4-ad03e419f6fc), tenant diversus.com.au. Front Door lives on MPN - devops (7d24c48d-a68e-46b7-9802-ff9d41879d14) in shared DWP-PROD RG. Trial deploy target: MPN - dtang sub (75f130b6-33d3-4c6a-b2a1-6d8c066df3b5), RG Huddler-Staging (empty).
2. Scope: ALL resources in HuddlerSubscriptionManager RG + ONLY the Front Door resource (HuddlerSubscriptionManagerFrontDoor) from DWP-PROD, combined into a SINGLE Bicep template deployable to one RG.
3. Layout: Apps/SubscriptionAndTelemetry/infra/ (empty folder already exists there next to the SubscriptionManager app code) - flat-ish (main.bicep + modules/*.bicep), not per-RG folders.
4. Inventory: final - no other resource groups planned beyond the above.
5. Secrets: @secure() params (not Key Vault) - currently no real secrets exist (Function App uses managed identity throughout; Logic App connections are OAuth-based tied to personal login, need manual re-auth regardless).
6. Front Door function-key rule: ALREADY CONFIGURED live (rule set SubscriptionManagerRules, rule AddFunctionKeyForSubscriptionManager, appends x-functions-key header on /api/getSubscriptionData) - just needs capturing in Bicep with key as @secure() param.
7. CI what-if on PRs: deferred to future work, to revisit at the end once Bicep exists.

Next step: begin the actual export/decompile workflow from the plan doc (docs/azure-iac-migration-plan.md) against HuddlerSubscriptionManager RG, plus separately exporting the Front Door resource from DWP-PROD, then hand-merge into Apps/SubscriptionAndTelemetry/infra/.

Progress: raw Bicep exports generated and committed (workspace1, branch task/20603-CreateBicepTemplateForSubscriptionManager, commit be18b2e3, not pushed). Apps/SubscriptionAndTelemetry/infra/main.raw.bicep (from HuddlerSubscriptionManager RG) and frontdoor.raw.bicep (filtered export via --resource-ids of just the Front Door profile+endpoint+origin group+rule set+route from shared DWP-PROD RG). Note: az group export needs -o tsv or it wraps output as an escaped JSON string. docs/azure-iac-migration-plan.md intentionally left uncommitted (excluded per Josh's request) - remember to handle that file separately later. Also: repo uses commitlint/husky requiring conventional commit format 'type(scope): subject' - plain messages get rejected silently (exit 1, no commit made) unless format matches. Next: manual cleanup pass - merge main.raw.bicep + frontdoor.raw.bicep into one template, extract params, split into modules, fix dependsOn, make Front Door key a @secure() param.

Changed approach: instead of a separate log file, we're extending docs/azure-iac-migration-plan.md itself with 'Pre-work decisions (resolved)' and 'Progress log' sections, and committing it incrementally as we go (commit c5475ad0, 'docs(subscription): add pre-work decisions and progress log to Azure IaC migration plan', not pushed). This doc is now tracked/committed going forward (no longer excluded).

Big progress: wrote and validated the cleaned-up Bicep template. Apps/SubscriptionAndTelemetry/infra/main.bicep + modules/{storageAccount,appInsights,functionApp,logicApps,monitoring,frontDoor}.bicep. Committed as bf905aeb (not pushed). Key points:
- Explicit appSettings block added (missing from raw export) - all 8 settings derived from other resources, no secrets.
- 2 real secrets found and made @secure(): Logic App bypassOriginCheck GUID key, Front Door function key.
- Front Door origin hostName now references functionApp module's defaultHostName output instead of a hardcoded non-portable string.
- Front Door module uses module-level scope (resourceGroup(subId, rgName)) parameterized via frontDoorSubscriptionId/frontDoorResourceGroupName - defaults to 'same RG as everything else' (for Huddler-Staging single-RG trial per decision 2), overridable to the real DWP-PROD/devops sub for validation.
- Dropped noise: stale sites/deployments history, ~30 default ProactiveDetectionConfigs, auto-managed functions/hostNameBindings child resources.
- Ran az deployment group what-if against real HuddlerSubscriptionManager RG (Front Door scoped to real DWP-PROD). Found + fixed a real gap: storageAccount queueServices/default classic 'logging' block (all disabled, v1.0) was missing from raw export and my first draft - added it back. Remaining diff: benign additive immutableStorageWithVersioning property on 3 containers (present in raw export too, harmless).
- KNOWN LIMITATION: what-if could not evaluate Logic Apps/connections/server farm/Function App site/Front Door module at all (NestedDeploymentShortCircuited) since they depend on runtime outputs from earlier modules. Real validation of those parts requires an actual deploy, i.e. the Huddler-Staging trial.
Next: trial-deploy the combined template into Huddler-Staging (dtang sub), confirm it comes up correctly end-to-end.

REMINDER for after the Huddler-Staging trial deploy succeeds: remove/simplify the what-if invocation that specifies frontDoorSubscriptionId/frontDoorResourceGroupName pointing at the real separate DWP-PROD/devops subscription (that override was only for validating against the current split-across-two-RGs reality). Once Huddler-Staging trial proves out, Huddler-Staging becomes the reference single-RG deployment, and that same single-RG deployment approach should then be used to deploy prod too (i.e. stop treating Front Door as living in a separate RG/subscription going forward - collapse to one RG for real deployments, matching decision 2's original intent).

Blocked/paused on the trial deploy: Microsoft.Cdn provider not registered on MPN - dtang sub (75f130b6-...), and my account got AuthorizationFailed trying to register it there. Decision made (not yet executed): switch the trial to MPN - devops sub (7d24c48d-a68e-46b7-9802-ff9d41879d14) instead, which already has Microsoft.Cdn available (hosts the real prod Front Door). Plan: create a NEW 'Huddler-Staging' RG on that subscription (doesn't exist yet - only DWP-PROD and Huddler-Igloo currently there), and deploy the FULL combined template (storage, function app, logic apps, monitoring, AND a brand new Front Door) into that single RG - not touching the real prod resources. Josh will try to resolve the Cdn provider registration on dtang in parallel, separately. Still to do when resumed: 1) create Huddler-Staging RG on devops sub, 2) run real deploy with storageAccountName override (huddlersubscriptionstg - confirmed globally available), logAnalyticsWorkspaceId/smartDetectionActionGroupId (likely reuse jhollander sub's real ones cross-subscription, same tenant), bypassOriginCheckKey (new value for trial), frontDoorFunctionKey (placeholder first pass, then real key fetched after Function App exists, second pass), 3) after success, per earlier note, simplify main.bicep to drop the cross-RG Front Door scope override and use single-RG shape for real deployments including prod.

While paused waiting on Microsoft.Cdn/subscription-assignment blocker, did a naming/tags/cleanup pass on the Bicep template (all committed: b6d4755e, 305bb6de, 57997b2f, 2c8ad20d, 44ff584b). Key changes:
- Dropped the CAF <type>-huddler-<feature> naming idea; went with plain kebab-case names + tags instead (storage account stays lowercase-only, no hyphens).
- Standard tags on all taggable resources: Practice=Modern Workplace, Product=Huddler, Module=Subscription. huddler-telemetry App Insights component gets Module=Telemetry instead (shared/broader resource).
- Removed unused SyncSubscriptionTables Logic App + 3 unused API connections (sharepointonline, sharepointonline-1, azuretables) - none were referenced by the remaining UpdateFrontDoorCache Logic App. Kept only azuretables-1 (renamed subscriptions-table-connection).
- Removed the Failure Anomalies smart detector rule for the shared huddler-telemetry component (kept the one for subscription-manager-insights).
- All locations now derive from resourceGroup().location consistently (previously mixed w/ hardcoded northcentralus); Front Door profile/endpoint stay hardcoded 'Global' (Azure hard requirement, not a choice).
- Final resource names all applied to main.bicep param defaults - see plan doc 'Naming convention and tags' section for the full before/after table.
Also: Josh discovered the dtang subscription was the WRONG one - staging and prod RGs are getting NEW subscriptions assigned. So the Huddler-Staging trial (and the whole subscription-pivot-to-devops plan) is on hold until that's sorted, in addition to the Microsoft.Cdn provider registration issue.

Microsoft.Cdn blocker RESOLVED: registered on MPN - dtang sub (75f130b6-...) - a CDN was provisioned there to trigger it. Huddler-Staging and Huddler-Prod RGs both already exist there (australiaeast), both empty. All other required providers confirmed still registered. STAYING ON DTANG (the earlier 'wrong subscription'/devops-pivot plan is no longer needed). Committed as a5c2e996. Ready next session: attempt real trial deploy into Huddler-Staging on dtang, Front Door collapsed into same single RG (no scope override needed). Still need to sort before deploying: logAnalyticsWorkspaceId/smartDetectionActionGroupId for this subscription (fresh, no default workspace/action group exist yet), fresh bypassOriginCheckKey, and placeholder-then-real frontDoorFunctionKey two-pass approach.

items.text: Check if Ubuntu kernel Bluetooth regression is fixed, then re-run GRUB default to latest kernel

notes.text: Bug: MediaTek MT7922 Bluetooth NULL pointer deref (btmtk_usb_hci_wmt_sync / btmtk_setup_firmware_79xx / __pm_runtime_resume) in kernel 6.8.0-139-generic on Ubuntu/Mint noble base. Regression from 6.8.0-138 (good). Laptop: ASUS Vivobook K6602ZC. Tracked upstream at Launchpad bug #2166561 (https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/2166561), status New as of 2026-09-07, plus duplicates #2166487/#2166497/#2166509/#2166544/#2166569/#2166577 - none fixed yet. Currently pinned GRUB_DEFAULT to boot 6.8.0-138-generic (via /etc/default/grub, saved advanced-options submenu entry) as a workaround. When check apt (apt list --upgradable | grep linux-image) shows a kernel newer than 6.8.0-139 available AND Launchpad bug 2166561 status is Fix Released, update system, then reset /etc/default/grub GRUB_DEFAULT back to 0 (or remove pin) and run 'sudo update-grub' to resume booting the latest kernel.

STATUS UPDATE 2026-09-07: GRUB has been pinned to boot 6.8.0-138-generic by default (workaround applied and confirmed working - Bluetooth fully functional, headphones reconnected). Change made via: sudo sed -i on /etc/default/grub setting GRUB_DEFAULT="gnulinux-advanced-3d825b06-2dc5-4f9e-86a8-c4e9d8e181d7>gnulinux-6.8.0-138-generic-advanced-3d825b06-2dc5-4f9e-86a8-c4e9d8e181d7" then 'sudo update-grub'. Backup of original config at /etc/default/grub.bak (had GRUB_DEFAULT=0). Confirmed applied: 'sudo grep -n default= /boot/grub/grub.cfg' shows 'set default="gnulinux-advanced-...>gnulinux-6.8.0-138-generic-advanced-..."' on line 29. TO REVERT once fixed: edit /etc/default/grub, set GRUB_DEFAULT=0 (or restore from grub.bak), then run 'sudo update-grub' again. Check fix status via: apt list --upgradable | grep linux-image (look for kernel newer than 6.8.0-139), and check https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/2166561 for status change from 'New' to 'Fix Released'.

STATUS UPDATE 2 (2026-09-07): Abandoned the GRUB_DEFAULT approach - it didn't reliably take effect on reboot (booted 6.8.0-139 again despite grub.cfg showing the correct default entry, cause not fully diagnosed - possibly recordfail/hidden-timeout interaction). Instead used Update Manager's Linux Kernels GUI to fully UNINSTALL linux-image-6.8.0-139-generic (+ its modules/modules-extra) while booted into 6.8.0-138-generic. Confirmed via dpkg -l and /boot/vmlinuz-* listing that 139 is gone and 138 is now the newest installed kernel; bluetoothctl/hciconfig confirm Bluetooth fully working. This means GRUB now naturally boots 138 without needing any default-entry override (simpler and more robust). Also checked: Update Manager's other kernel series options (6.11, 6.14, 6.17) are marked 'end of life' (no security updates) so were NOT used; 7.0 is supported/'superseded' like 6.8 but was not tried since 6.8.0-138 already works. REMAINING TODO: still periodically check apt list --upgradable | grep linux-image for a new kernel >6.8.0-139, and check https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/2166561 for status change to Fix Released. Once a fixed kernel is available and installed via Update Manager, no GRUB changes are needed (nothing to revert) - just let the new kernel become the default naturally, then optionally remove 6.8.0-138 once confirmed fixed. NOTE: /etc/default/grub still has the leftover GRUB_DEFAULT override pointing at the now-removed 6.8.0-138-generic advanced entry - this should be reset to GRUB_DEFAULT=0 (or restore /etc/default/grub.bak) + sudo update-grub at some point to clean up, though it's currently harmless since 138 is the only/newest kernel anyway.

STATUS UPDATE 3 (2026-09-07): Reset /etc/default/grub GRUB_DEFAULT back to 0 (normal 'boot newest kernel' behavior) + sudo update-grub, since it's no longer needed now that 6.8.0-139 is fully uninstalled. Confirmed grub.cfg regenerated cleanly with 6.8.0-138-generic as the newest available kernel. System is now in a clean, simple state: no custom GRUB overrides, just naturally boots 138. Nothing further needed until a fixed kernel appears - just check apt/Launchpad bug 2166561 periodically per earlier notes.
